info.name: Ticket Booking - Phase 8 (idempotency, async payment, webhook, notifications)
info.description:
Ticket Booking API, Phase 8: idempotency keys, async payment with webhook, and email notifications. Important requests only, for one organizer and one user.

HOW TO RUN
1. Start everything: the databases, Kafka, config-server, eureka-server, user-service, cinema-service, payment-service, booking-service, notification-service, then api-gateway. Wait about 30 seconds so every service shows up in Eureka.
2. Use the COLLECTION RUNNER (or Newman), not single Send. The poll requests repeat themselves until the async result arrives, and that works only in the runner.
3. Almost every request goes through the API Gateway (baseUrl, port 8080). Only folder 7 (webhook checks) goes straight to the Payment service, so set paymentServiceUrl to its real port.
4. The organizer is created by DevDataSeeder in user-service: organizer@ticket.com, password Organizer@123.
5. Config the folders rely on (payment-service config):
   payment.gateway.async-enabled: true
   payment.gateway.webhook-delay-ms: 2000
   payment.gateway.max-amount: 10000
   payment.webhook.secret must equal the webhookSecret variable below (default dev-only-secret).
6. Run the folders in order. Tokens and ids are saved into collection variables by the test scripts.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE PHASE 6
- POST /bookings and POST /payments need an Idempotency-Key header. A repeat with the same key returns the same result (no second booking or charge). The same key with a different body gives 422.
- POST /bookings returns 201 with status PENDING at once. The final status (CONFIRMED, REJECTED, PAYMENT_FAILED) comes later, so the collection polls GET /bookings/{id}.
- The fake gateway answers PENDING, then calls POST /api/v1/webhooks/payment about 2 seconds later with an X-Signature. Folder 7 sends signed and unsigned webhooks by hand (the signature is calculated in each pre-request script).
- Cancel returns CANCELLED at once. Seats and the refund follow through Kafka, so they are polled too.

NOTIFICATIONS (no public endpoint, so check by hand after a run)
SELECT booking_id, type, status, recipient FROM notification_logs ORDER BY id DESC;
Expect BOOKING_CONFIRMED, BOOKING_FAILED (the REJECTED booking and the PAYMENT_FAILED booking) and BOOKING_CANCELLED rows, all SENT, with the recipient set to userEmail. The Notification service log also prints each "EMAIL to ..." line.

Re-running is safe: registration accepts 201 or 409, and each run creates a new movie, new shows and new idempotency keys.

item.name: Register user (201, or 409 if already registered)

exec: pm.test("201 created, or 409 if already registered", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([201, 409]); });
pm.test("no password or hash in response", function () { pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property("password"); pm.expect(b).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });
pm.test("has access and refresh token", function () { pm.expect(b.accessToken).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(b.refreshToken).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(b.tokenType).to.eql("Bearer"); });
pm.test("has access and refresh token", function () { pm.expect(b.accessToken).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(b.refreshToken).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(b.tokenType).to.eql("Bearer"); });
pm.test("token role is USER", function () { pm.expect(claims.role).to.eql("USER"); });
// one week from now, so the start time is always in the future
pm.test("contains the new show", function () { const ids = pm.response.json().map(function (s) { return String(s.id); }); pm.expect(ids).to.include(String(pm.collectionVariables.get("showId"))); });
pm.test("message names the missing header", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include("Idempotency-Key"); });

item.name: Create booking with a key (201, PENDING)

exec: // a new unique key for every run
pm.test("booking is PENDING, the user does not wait for payment", function () { pm.expect(b.status).to.eql("PENDING"); });
pm.test("owner comes from the token", function () { pm.expect(String(b.userId)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("userId")); });

item.name: Repeat the same request, same key (201, same booking)

exec: pm.test("same booking id, no second booking created", function () { pm.expect(String(b.id)).to.eql(String(pm.collectionVariables.get("bookingId"))); });
pm.test("message says the key was used with a different request", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include("different request"); });
// wait 1.5 s before each try, the result arrives asynchronously (webhook, Kafka)
// still processing: run this same request again (works in the Collection Runner and Newman)
pm.test("booking is CONFIRMED after the webhook", function () { pm.expect(b.status).to.eql("CONFIRMED"); });
pm.test("payment id is returned", function () { pm.expect(b.paymentId).to.be.a("number"); });
pm.test("total is price x 2 seats", function () { pm.expect(Number(b.totalAmount)).to.eql(500); });
const mine = seats.filter(function (s) { return s.id == pm.collectionVariables.get("seatId1") || s.id == pm.collectionVariables.get("seatId2"); });
pm.test("both seats are BOOKED", function () { pm.expect(mine.length).to.eql(2); mine.forEach(function (s) { pm.expect(s.status).to.eql("BOOKED"); }); });
